newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER AHEAD OF HOLIDAY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES FIRMER AHEAD OF HOLIDAY.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed Thursday's interbank session firmer against most hard currencies ahead of the country's Independence holiday on Friday.
"I think we got quite a bit of money coming into the market today...I'm not quite sure whether it was from the (central) Reserve Bank or from other sources," one dealer commented.
In the morning, another dealer said: "I suspect the money is coming from tobacco companies trying to capitalise on the depreciation of the Zimbabwe dollar over the last few days."

Market analysts have predicted an appreciatory trend in the local unit when foreign currency starts flowing in from the annual tobacco auctions set to open later this month. They say some of the proceeds have already started trickling in.
The Zimbabwe dollar finished on Thursday at 11.2975/3075 against the U.S. dollar from 11.3100/3200 overnight and was also quoted firmer on the mark at 6.5390/5480 compared with 6.5525/5620 overnight.
It was at 2.5290/5330 from 2.5370/5410 against the rand but slipped versus sterling to 18.3865/4130 from 18.3450/3650.
